claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the exported greatest-common-divisor function returns their unsigned greatest common divisor encoded as a 32-bit result.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: For every pair of unsigned 32-bit inputs, the result is their greatest common divisor, including when either input is zero, as the examples illustrate.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Covers every pair of 32-bit bit-vector inputs, passed to the export as two i32 values.
Both inputs are interpreted as unsigned natural numbers for the greatest-common-divisor calculation; the result is encoded back into 32 bits, with `ofNat` reducing modulo 2 to the 32nd power.

`Returns` additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and that every call, under every host behavior and from every fresh instance, terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified single i32 result.
caveats: The guarantee is conditional on the elaborated expression: it uses each 32-bit input's unsigned natural-number interpretation, not signed integers. The source spelling `Nat.gcd` is the elaborated `toNat.gcd`.
No example executions or implementation details are supplied; this is a universal input/output guarantee, not a description of the algorithm.

claims.summary: For every triple of 32-bit inputs, the exported clamp function returns the value selected by its ordered signed comparisons against the two bounds.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Rust.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: The signed comparisons return the lower bound when x is below it, the upper bound when x is above it, and x otherwise, matching the stated behavior, including when the bounds are reversed.
claims.name: Examples.Rust.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: Covers every triple of 32-bit bit-vector inputs, passed as i32 values: the candidate value, lower bound, and upper bound.

Comparisons use signed 32-bit interpretation. It returns the lower bound if the candidate is below it; otherwise it returns the upper bound if that bound is below the candidate; otherwise it returns the candidate.
The selected input is returned unchanged as an i32, so there is no arithmetic wraparound in the selection.

`Returns` additionally guarantees that the module can be instantiated and that every call, under every host behavior and from every fresh instance, terminates without trapping and returns exactly the specified single i32 result.
caveats: The condition is a nested signed comparison, not an assumption that the lower bound is at most the upper bound; when bounds are reversed, the expression still follows the stated comparison order.
The result is exactly one of the supplied 32-bit inputs; the claim says nothing about memory effects or other exports.
